title: She Won the 50-Over World Cup. Now Harmanpreet Wants the One Trophy That Has Always Escaped Her.
excerpt: India open their Women's T20 World Cup campaign against Pakistan at Edgbaston on Sunday — with a maiden T20 title in their sights
body:
She has won the 50-over World Cup. She has led India to three T20 World Cup semi-finals. On Sunday, at the ground where she once scored the most famous 171 in women's cricket history, Harmanpreet Kaur will walk out for another India-Pakistan opener — this time, as the reigning world champion chasing the one trophy she has never lifted.

India begin their ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 campaign against Pakistan at Edgbaston, Birmingham, on June 14. The match starts at 2:30 PM local time (7:00 PM IST, 9:30 AM ET, 6:30 AM PT). For NRIs across the US, that means an early Sunday alarm — but for a rivalry that transcends rankings and form, few will mind.

## The Weight of History

India have won eight of nine T20I meetings against Pakistan. Their only loss came in the 2022 Asia Cup — a result that still stings. At the 2024 T20 World Cup in Dubai, India won by six wickets in a match that drew the highest digital viewership in women's cricket history.

But these numbers rarely matter when the two sides meet. Pakistan's captain Fatima Sana, despite a right knee injury sustained in practice, is expected to lead her team into the contest. If she is ruled out, it could shift the dynamic — but Pakistan have shown in the past that the tournament stage amplifies their fight, not their limitations.

"The first game is very important; it always sets the tone," Kaur said on the eve of the match. "Winning the World Cup was a great moment for all of us. We were waiting for that moment for so many years, and it's good to see years of hard work pay off."

## The Reigning Champions Want More

India arrive in England as reigning ODI World Cup champions after their historic 2025 triumph. The T20 World Cup title, however, has eluded them — and this squad knows it. The roster blends experience and firepower: Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma at the top, Jemimah Rodrigues in the middle order, and Richa Ghosh providing explosive finishing power after a blistering half-century in the warm-up against England.

The bowling attack features Renuka Singh Thakur's swing, Deepti Sharma's miserly control, and the spin duo of Shreyanka Patil and Radha Yadav. In English conditions where the ball moves early and spinners operate through the middle overs, India's balance looks formidable.

India's probable XI: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Richa Ghosh (wk), Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Renuka Thakur, Radha Yadav.

## Pakistan's Puncher's Chance

Pakistan are eighth in the T20I rankings, and their build-up has been far from smooth. But their bowling — anchored by spin stalwarts Sadia Iqbal and Nida Dar — has the quality to restrict India's middle order, particularly if Edgbaston's surface offers grip. The venue has averaged a run rate of just 6.55 in women's T20Is over the past four years, suggesting this will not be a flat-track shootout.

"Whenever we play against Pakistan, pressure is going to be there," Harmanpreet acknowledged. "But these two practice games have given us a lot of confidence."

## Birmingham's Desi Crowd

Edgbaston has long been a fortress for subcontinental cricket fans. Birmingham's sizeable South Asian community — one of the largest in England — has a tradition of turning India-Pakistan matches into electric occasions. For NRIs in the UK, this is the marquee fixture of the group stage. Tickets have been in high demand since the draw was announced.

## Where NRIs Can Watch

Indian fans can catch the match on Star Sports channels, with JioHotstar live-streaming the game. In the US, Willow TV carries ICC events. Unite8 Sports, the ZEE5 app, and DD Sports offer additional broadcast options for viewers in India and select international markets.

## What's at Stake

India are third in the T20I rankings and are chasing their first-ever Women's T20 World Cup title. The tournament runs from June 12 to July 5 across seven venues in England. After Pakistan, India face the Netherlands (June 17, Headingley) and South Africa (June 21, Old Trafford) in Group 1 — a group where a fast start is not optional but essential.

For Pakistan, a result here would be transformational. They have never reached a T20 World Cup semi-final and enter the tournament as underdogs. But on this stage, against this opponent, form is irrelevant. It always has been.
